definition: full of people, with little space to move
example: The train was really {{crowded}} this morning.
example2: Let's go early before the beach gets crowded.

definition: to slowly make something weaker or less likely to succeed
example: Constant criticism can {{undermine}} a new employee's confidence.
example2: Rumors about the plan undermined the team's trust in the manager.

definition: feeling good because something nice has happened
example: I am {{happy}} because today is Friday.
example2: The children are happy to see the dog.

definition: a person who works at a school and helps students learn
example: My {{teacher}} is very kind.
example2: The teacher writes a word on the board.

definition: a person who lives in the next house or apartment
example: My {{neighbor}} has a very friendly dog.
example2: We said hello to our new neighbors.

definition: the bags and cases you take with you on a trip
example: Please put your {{luggage}} on the shelf.
example2: Our luggage got lost at the airport.

definition: having a lot of things to do
example: My father is {{busy}} on weekdays.
example2: I was busy yesterday, so I did not call you.

definition: large, heavy or slow in a way that is hard to handle
example: The old software was {{cumbersome}} and hard to use.
example2: The cumbersome rules slowed down every project.

definition: to move an event to a later time
example: They had to {{postpone}} the meeting until next week.
example2: The game was postponed because of the rain.

definition: to discuss something formally to reach a deal
example: They {{negotiated}} for weeks before signing the contract.
example2: We're negotiating a lower price with the supplier.

definition: to tell someone that a person or thing is good and worth choosing
example: Can you {{recommend}} a good dentist near here?
example2: The doctor recommended more rest and plenty of water.

definition: to ask someone to come to a party or event
example: She {{invited}} twenty friends to her birthday party.
example2: Thank you for inviting me.

definition: real enough to be seen, touched or clearly measured
example: The new tool brought {{tangible}} benefits within a month.
example2: There is no tangible proof of the claim.

meanings.ja: 具体的な・目に見える

definition: seeming likely to be true or reasonable
example: His excuse sounded {{plausible}}, but nobody could check it.
example2: That is a plausible explanation for the delay.

definition: an agreement where each side accepts less than it wanted
example: After a long discussion, we finally reached a {{compromise}}.
example2: Every good relationship needs some compromise.

definition: so unclear that it fails to settle a question either way
example: The senator gave an {{equivocal}} answer to a simple question.
example2: The test results were equivocal, so the doctor ordered another one.

meanings.ja: あいまいな・どちらとも取れる

definition: ready for you to use, buy or meet at a particular time
example: Only two seats are still {{available}} on Thursday's flight.
example2: The new phone will be available in stores next month.

meanings.ja: 利用できる・空いている

definition: a person you like and enjoy spending time with
example: Ken is my best {{friend}}.
example2: I play soccer with my friends on Sunday.

definition: describing things that seem to have nothing in common with each other
example: The team merged {{disparate}} ideas into one clear plan.
example2: She studied disparate fields, from music to biology.

definition: too eager to please someone powerful, in a way that seems fake
example: The {{obsequious}} assistant laughed at every joke his boss told.
example2: I found his obsequious bow embarrassing.

definition: not costing much money
example: This shirt was {{cheap}}, only five dollars.
example2: We found a cheap hotel near the station.

definition: wanting to eat food
example: I am {{hungry}}, so I want some rice.
example2: The hungry dog ate all of its food.

definition: something with handles that you use to carry your things
example: She put her book in her {{bag}}.
example2: My bag is under the table.

definition: wanting to drink water or tea
example: I am {{thirsty}} after the soccer game.
example2: I get thirsty when I walk in the sun.

definition: to get ready for something that will happen soon
example: I need to {{prepare}} for tomorrow's big meeting.
example2: Are you prepared for tomorrow's test?

definition: easy to use, or suitable for your plans
example: Would Tuesday afternoon be {{convenient}} for you?
example2: The hotel is in a convenient location near the station.

definition: having nothing inside
example: The box was {{empty}} when I opened it.
example2: Please don't leave the empty bottles on the table.

definition: behaving in a kind way that shows respect for other people
example: It is {{polite}} to say thank you when someone helps you.
example2: The waiter was polite even when the guests were rude.

definition: holding on to a goal and refusing to let go, even when it is hard
example: The {{tenacious}} reporter kept asking questions until she got an answer.
example2: Our tenacious goalkeeper saved three shots in the final minute.

definition: to take something from someone and give it back later
example: Can I {{borrow}} your pen for a second?
example2: She borrowed three books from the library.

definition: possible to do and likely to work in practice
example: The plan sounds good, but is it {{feasible}}?
example2: A feasible schedule leaves time for mistakes.

definition: certain to happen, whatever anyone does to stop it
example: With so much snow, delays were {{inevitable}}.
example2: Change is inevitable in any growing company.

definition: expected to explain your decisions and accept the results
example: Managers are {{accountable}} for their team's mistakes.
example2: Who will be held accountable for the delay?

definition: to make a harmful effect or problem less severe
example: Planting trees can {{mitigate}} the effects of heavy flooding.
example2: The company added extra staff to mitigate the risk of delays.

definition: to offer an idea or plan for someone to consider
example: Can I {{suggest}} a different time for the meeting?
example2: She suggested that we take the train.

definition: stubbornly refusing to obey rules or follow orders
example: The {{recalcitrant}} student ignored every warning from the teacher.
example2: The committee was recalcitrant and rejected all offers.

meanings.ja: 反抗的な・手に負えない

definition: a small piece of paper that lets you enter a place or ride a train
example: Can I have one {{ticket}} to Kyoto?
example2: Do you have your train ticket?

definition: having more than one possible meaning, so it is unclear
example: His reply was so {{ambiguous}} that nobody knew whether he agreed.
example2: The contract's wording is ambiguous, so we should ask a lawyer.

definition: the meal you eat in the morning
example: I eat {{breakfast}} at seven every day.
example2: Do you want toast for breakfast?

definition: using very few words, sometimes in a way that seems blunt
example: His {{laconic}} reply, just "Fine," told us nothing.
example2: The laconic farmer answered every question with a nod.

definition: sad because you have no friends or people near you
example: My grandmother feels {{lonely}} since she moved to a new town.
example2: He was lonely in the big city at first.

definition: not wanting to do something and slow to agree to it
example: She was {{reluctant}} to ask her boss for help.
example2: Many people are reluctant to change their habits.

definition: money that a shop gives back when you return something you bought
example: I asked for a {{refund}} because the shirt was too small.
example2: You'll get a full refund if you cancel today.

definition: measuring a lot from bottom to top, like a tree or a person
example: My brother is very {{tall}}.
example2: That is a tall building.

definition: the time or day by which something must be finished
example: We have to meet the {{deadline}} on Friday.
example2: I work best when a deadline is close.

definition: likely to change mood or mind suddenly for no clear reason
example: The {{capricious}} weather changed from sun to storm and back every hour.
example2: The king was capricious and often changed his orders.

definition: something you do often without thinking about it
example: Biting your nails is a bad {{habit}}.
example2: She has a habit of waking up at five.

definition: something that blocks your way or makes a goal hard to reach
example: Lack of money was the biggest {{obstacle}} to opening the cafe.
example2: A fallen tree was an obstacle on the road.

definition: to examine something very carefully to find any mistakes
example: Auditors {{scrutinize}} every receipt in the report.
example2: Voters scrutinized the candidate's past statements.

definition: a plan for a trip, with the places and times
example: I've emailed you the {{itinerary}} for our trip to Kyoto.
example2: Our itinerary includes two days in Osaka.

definition: feeling that there is too much to deal with
example: I felt completely {{overwhelmed}} during my first week at work.
example2: It's normal to feel overwhelmed when you move to a new city.

meanings.ja: 圧倒される・手に負えない

definition: to make a problem, pain or bad situation more severe
example: Skipping sleep will only {{exacerbate}} your headaches.
example2: The heavy rain exacerbated the flooding in the valley.

definition: good enough for a purpose, but not better than that
example: The old laptop is {{adequate}} for writing emails, but not for video editing.
example2: Adequate sleep helps you focus during the day.

definition: a person who buys things or services from a shop
example: The {{customer}} asked for a refund at the counter.
example2: Our customers love the new menu.

definition: to have something as a necessary part
example: The job will {{involve}} some travel abroad.
example2: Cooking for fifty people involves a lot of planning.

definition: feeling very upset because someone did something wrong
example: She was {{angry}} because her brother broke her phone.
example2: Please don't be angry with me.

definition: seeming to be present everywhere at the same time
example: Smartphones are now {{ubiquitous}}, even in remote villages.
example2: The company's logo is ubiquitous in this part of the city.

definition: to pause before you act because you feel unsure
example: Don't {{hesitate}} to call me if you have any questions.
example2: He hesitated at the door before knocking.

definition: to fail to remember something or someone
example: I always {{forget}} his name when we meet.
example2: Don't forget to lock the door.

definition: to admit that something is true, often after resisting
example: After an hour, he finally {{conceded}} that she was right.
example2: The team conceded defeat before the game ended.

definition: lasting for only a very brief time
example: Fame can be {{ephemeral}}, so save your money.
example2: The beauty of cherry blossoms is ephemeral.

meanings.ja: はかない・つかの間の

definition: having mixed feelings, both good and bad, about something
example: She felt {{ambivalent}} about moving abroad for the job.
example2: Voters remain ambivalent about the new law.

definition: to reach a final answer about what to do, after thinking
example: We couldn't {{decide}} where to eat, so we ordered pizza.
example2: Have you decided what to wear?

definition: always behaving or happening in the same way over time
example: She is a {{consistent}} performer who rarely misses a target.
example2: Your story is not consistent with what the video shows.

meanings.ja: 一貫した・矛盾のない

definition: not fake, but exactly what it is said to be
example: Is this bag made of {{genuine}} leather?
example2: Make sure the parts you buy are genuine.

definition: to fail to see something that is there
example: I {{overlooked}} a typo in the final report.
example2: Please don't overlook the small details.

definition: pleasant to wear or sit in, with nothing tight or hard
example: These shoes are really {{comfortable}}, even after a long walk.
example2: This sofa is very comfortable for reading.

definition: to reach something you wanted by working hard
example: She worked for years to {{achieve}} her dream.
example2: We achieved good results this quarter.

definition: a person's general feelings about something, shown in how they act
example: Her positive {{attitude}} made the long project easier.
example2: I don't like his attitude toward customers.

definition: a very small difference in meaning, tone or feeling
example: The translation missed the subtle {{nuance}} of her joke.
example2: He explained every nuance of the contract.

definition: a plan that lists the times when things will happen
example: I have a tight {{schedule}} this week, so let's meet on Friday.
example2: The train is running behind schedule today.

definition: to say that you are unhappy about something
example: Several guests {{complain}} about the noise from the street every weekend.
example2: She complained to the manager about the cold food.

definition: much more than a small amount, enough to matter
example: The company made a {{substantial}} profit this year.
example2: They received a substantial amount of help.

definition: to raise the quality of something, or to become higher in quality
example: She practices every day to {{improve}} her English.
example2: The weather should improve this afternoon.

definition: able to be trusted to work or act well
example: My car is old, but it's very {{reliable}}.
example2: Is this website a reliable source of news?

meanings.ja: 頼りになる・信頼できる

definition: done only because it is expected, without real care or interest
example: The manager gave a {{perfunctory}} apology and hurried away.
example2: Her thank-you was perfunctory, and nobody believed it.

definition: showing great care about every small detail
example: She keeps {{meticulous}} records of every purchase for tax season.
example2: The editor's meticulous work caught every tiny error.

definition: worried or a little afraid about something that is going to happen
example: I always get {{nervous}} before a job interview.
example2: He looked nervous on his first day at the new office.

definition: to use rules to keep an activity or amount small
example: The city will {{restrict}} cars in the old town on weekends.
example2: Doctors restrict his sugar intake.

definition: appearing to be the reason, though it may not be the real one
example: The {{ostensible}} purpose of the trip was a conference.
example2: His ostensible reason for leaving early was a headache.

definition: to have enough money to pay for something
example: We can't {{afford}} a new car this year.
example2: Can you afford to take a month off?

definition: caring more about what works than about ideals or theory
example: She took a {{pragmatic}} approach to the budget.
example2: Let's be pragmatic and choose the cheaper option.

definition: to make something clear by giving details
example: Can you {{explain}} how this machine works?
example2: He explained why he was late.
